rationale: A wins because it gives the founder more reporter-shaped, usable routes and an actual path to pitch. Its strongest headline, "Toast tells investors hardware is low-margin — the real bet is lending to the same 120,000 restaurants," turns the update into a testable public-company story; B's best line, "The number Toast won't give you: default rates on its restaurant cash advances," is sharp but then props itself up with the invented claim that the "prevailing belief" is a clean book. B also ends by punting to "newsjack-detector" because "there is no live news signal," which is process cosplay when the assignment was to make the update pitchable.
gaps_in_A: The payroll angle imports outside complexity without enough support: "tipped minimum wage variation by state, tip pooling rules, tip credits" may be true, but the update only says tipped and hourly staff.

The customer-power angle overstates lock-in: "what restaurant owners can't easily do about it" and "opting out of its financial products comes with real friction" need named operators or switching-cost evidence.

The investor and category angles overlap around the same margin thesis: "the real bet is lending" and "Vertical SaaS found its margin" are different altitudes, but they need cleaner separation or one will cannibalize the other.
gaps_in_B: The next step is wrong: "newsjack-detector — there is no live news signal in this update" punts instead of moving the strongest angles into proof-gathering or journalist fit.

The contrarian setup invents a strawman: "The prevailing belief is that a newly profitable, publicly traded platform lending against its own customers' sales has a clean, well-understood book" is not in the update.

The headline overstates the company move: "pivots from hardware to fintech margins" is stronger than the facts supplied, which say Toast is bundling lending and payroll and says fintech is higher-margin.

The refused payroll angle is dismissed for the wrong reason: calling it a "duplicate of the customer-story angle's protagonist" misses a distinct HR/workforce beat around tipped and hourly restaurant payroll.
